result.content:
# Proposed discovery plan

Determine whether to build and commercialize a dedicated handoff tracker for small software development teams in Latvia.

## Proposed scope

- Investigation of cross-functional and inter-role task handoff workflows in small software teams based in Latvia
- Evaluation of friction and time lost during recurring handoff updates and sprint transitions
- Exclusion: payroll, compensation tracking, or financial advisory functionality

Region: Latvia

Explicit exclusions: Do not include payroll or financial advice

## Engineering Lead

Responsible for sprint execution, developer workflows, and technical handoffs between developers and QA.

- How many hours per week does your engineering team spend compiling, copying, or communicating handoff status updates between team members? (question-53d1c65a830026bd506e800a)

## Product Operations Lead

Oversees delivery schedules, stakeholder reporting, and software tool selection for the team.

- What criteria or budget constraints would determine whether your team purchases a dedicated handoff tracker versus adapting existing project management software? (question-693c3574409474784a906286)

## Simulation hypotheses

- We spend two hours copying handoff updates each Friday. [source:operator-interview]

## Assumptions

- Small software teams in Latvia experience similar task transition inefficiencies as described in the synthetic interview fixture.
- A dedicated handoff tool could deliver enough value to justify a separate subscription without expanding into payroll or financial features.

## Evidence gaps

- No verified market data exists regarding the software tooling spend or addressable market size of small software development teams in Latvia.
- No empirical evidence showing whether two hours of weekly update copying is representative beyond the single synthetic transcript fixture.
- No non-synthetic source findings were established; the plan is a proposal, not customer validation.

This scope is proposed, not a claim of user approval.

## Selected sources

- [source:operator-interview] Synthetic operator interview fixture — synthetic_transcript
